subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose private-network access for arbitrary web_fetch URLs, and if so should the approved contract be global, per-agent, host-scoped, confirmation-based, or part of the broader egress-policy design?
rationale: The lower-level SSRF primitive exists, but exposing it to a model-callable URL fetch tool changes the security boundary and public config contract; automation cannot safely choose metadata, link-local, redirect, cache, provider-fallback, and requester-authorization semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a scoped SSRF policy
options.body: Land a reviewed default-off policy, preferably nested and scoped to trusted agents or hosts, with metadata/link-local blocks, redirect/cache safety, audit visibility, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Fold into broader egress controls
options.body: Defer private-network access until the hostname allowlist and network access-control work define one coherent policy for web_fetch egress.

options.title: Keep arbitrary web_fetch strict
options.body: Reject broad private-network access for arbitrary web_fetch and document supported alternatives such as trusted proxies, browser policy, or explicit plugin/tool integrations.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped SSRF policy
recommendation.body: Land a reviewed default-off policy, preferably nested and scoped to trusted agents or hosts, with metadata/link-local blocks, redirect/cache safety, audit visibility, docs, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the most specific maintainer-context comment tying this issue to the remaining security-sensitive config decision and has repeated SSRF/web_fetch history.
